title: Charge Review Cycle and Borrower Notice Settings — Set-Aside Accounts
content:
Plans of Set-Aside Accounts that pay or fund property charges keep the annual charges on file under periodic review and send the borrower notices about the balance. The settings by plan are:

| Plan | Review interval for the annual charges on file (months) | Document that supports an update to the annual charges | Low-balance notice when the balance is projected to cover fewer than this many months of the charges it pays | Calendar days after depletion within which the borrower is told the charges are now theirs to pay |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fully Funded LESA (Mandatory) | 12 | The tax bill or the insurance declaration page | 12 | 10 |
| Fully Funded LESA (Borrower-Elected) | 12 | The tax bill or the insurance declaration page | 12 | 10 |
| Partially Funded LESA | 12 | The tax bill or the insurance declaration page | 6 | 10 |
| Repair Set-Aside | 0 (pays no charges) | Not applicable | 0 (no projection notice) | 0 (not applicable) |
| Servicing Fee Set-Aside | 0 (pays no charges) | Not applicable | 0 (no projection notice) | 0 (not applicable) |
| Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve | 12 | The tax bill or the insurance declaration page | 12 | 10 |

## Reading the settings

- A review interval of 12 means the annual charges on file are reviewed every 12 months; a 0 means the plan pays no property charges and has no review cycle.
- **Hypothetical low-balance test.** For a plan with a 12-month notice setting, a balance of 3,000.00 against charges of 4,800.00 a year covers 7.5 months of charges, fewer than 12, so a low-balance notice applies. A balance covering 13 months of charges under the same setting would not reach the notice point.
- **Depletion notice.** Where the setting is 10, a set-aside that depletes on a given date is followed by the notice no later than the tenth calendar day after that date.
